results.evidence: Live row re-read 2026-10-01: gain_ft null, loss_ft null, dist_km null; approach, itinerary and waypoints all describe Wolf Creek Trail #527 -> Gardner Meadows -> tarn -> spur ridge -> north ridge. Sources read this pass: (1) SummitPost Abernathy Peak page (Wayback 2024 copy), Route 3 Wolf Creek: trailhead 'at 2,400 ft', 11 mi to Gardner Meadows (c. 5,700 ft), 'two miles to the 7,680+ ft saddle', '3,300 ft of gain from trailhead to meadows, then 2,700 ft more to the top'. It states only two legs, no total; adding them would be computing. Its 2,400 ft trailhead also disagrees with the row's ~3,000 ft (USGS 2,997) trailhead. Its Route 2 North Creek gives '4,700 ft of gain', confirming the old 4,660 belonged to the North Creek line. (2) countryhighpoints 'Abernathy and the Gardners' (Wolf Creek, north ridge): only a whole-day 34 mi / 8,000 ft across three peaks. (3) countryhighpoints winter ascents (Wolf Creek, north ridge above Nasty Pond): only 30 mi skiing / 8 mi snowmobiling for three peaks, no gain. (4) mountainflamingo 2015: Scatter Creek ascent, out by Wolf Creek, 20.9 mi / 11,500 ft across three peaks. (5) Search excerpts: trail-only figures (21.0 mi RT and 4,270 ft for the Wolf Creek trail; 19.6 mi and 3,681 ft to Gardner Meadows; 'starts at about 2900' and gains 2400' to Gardner Meadows') cover the trail, not the summit. (6) Peakbagger ascent list (Wayback 2020): the logged gains (3,154; 5,122) are south-side ascents; no Wolf Creek ascent with a gain was visible. (7) whereiskylemiller and hike2hike: Scatter Lake side. (8) The 2020 WTA overnight report via Wolf Creek: 403 and no Wayback copy. Result: no stated trailhead-to-summit gain for this line from even one source. The row's fitnessSpec 'roughly 2,600 ft from the meadows' is a difference of two stated heights (s3) and sits within SummitPost's 2,700, so it needs no change.
